What's really happening under your rug

Why spraying alone never works

A rug isn't one layer, it's five: wool fibers, woven jute backing, adhesive, padding and the subfloor. Cat pee soaks through every one of them.

Cat pee, not honey!
The problem

Would somebody please explain why you'd ever add more liquid to THIS?!

Urine sinks from the fibers through the backing and padding, all the way to the subfloor. Spraying more liquid on top just pushes the mess deeper, where it waits for the next humid day.

THIS is how you get to the bottom of it!

Powder Fusion pulls moisture and uric acid crystals up through every layer and locks them in, so you vacuum the mess out instead of driving it down.

Step 2 · Enzyme Fusion

THIS is the kiss that seals the deal!

Bio-enzymes eat the residue and odor markers left behind, so there's nothing for your cat's nose, or the humidity, to bring back.

Using the system

Why do I need a 2-step system? Can't I just spray something and pretend the accident never happened?

You could, but you'd be faking the funk! Spraying a wet mess without lifting the uric acid crystals first just creates a nasty chemical soup deep in your rug padding. Step 1: Shady Cat Powder Fusion locks down and lifts out the bulk of the physical crystals. Step 2: Shady Cat Enzyme Fusion is the final eviction notice, moving in to eat up any microscopic residue left behind. Teamwork makes the clean work!

I brushed the Powder Fusion deep down into my rug. Is it just going to live down there forever now?

Absolutely not. We didn't build a carpet graveyard! Our powder acts like an army of microscopic magnets. It dives down, finds the wet uric acid crystals and locks them inside a dry, hollow sphere. Once dry, its grip on your carpet fibers is completely broken. When you run your vacuum over it, the brush roll vibrates the fibers, lifting those encapsulated crystals straight to the top and sucking them away for good.

What happens if I skip the wet rag step for the Enzyme Fusion spray?

Think of the wet rag as a cozy blanket for our bio-enzymes. They need moisture and a little time to wake up, multiply and get hungry enough to feast on those stubborn, invisible organic stains. If you skip the rag, they dry out too fast and go back to sleep. Give them 30 minutes under the rag, and they'll destroy the funk for good!

Can I use this system on my mattress or couch, or is it strictly a carpet-only situation?

It works beautifully across almost all porous fabrics! If your chaotic fur baby decided your mattress, couch cushions, pillows or even the pile of dirty laundry was their backup litter box, this 2-step system is your absolute lifesaver. Just follow the exact same routine to lock, lift and destroy the grime on basically any fabric surface in your home. Now, if your cat actually peed on the family hamster? We love you, but you're on your own with that family meeting! For everything else, we've got you covered. No one wants to head to bed and feel like they're sleeping inside a giant litter box!

My cat had a little accident on the kitchen tile. Can I use the enzyme spray there?

Absolutely! While the powder is reserved for soft, porous surfaces like rugs and fabrics, our enzyme spray is a multi-talented superstar. It can be used on hard surfaces like wood, vinyl flooring, tile and especially the grout. Just spray the area to let the bio-enzymes break down and feast on those invisible organic odor markers, wipe it clean and enjoy a completely fresh space!

I used the system, but I still see a faint "halo" ring left behind. Did it fail?

Our formula doesn't lose battles, but liquid messes are deceptively wide! Liquid spreads out under a carpet like an upside-down mushroom. If a halo ring appears, it just means the hidden puddle underneath was slightly larger than you anticipated, or a little more product was needed to reach the outer perimeter. Don't sweat it. Simply re-apply the system a few inches wider than the ring, use a generous amount of product to saturate the area completely and watch that shadow pull a vanishing act!

Can I use Powder Fusion in the litter box?

Nope! Powder Fusion is a cleaning product, not a litter-box deodorizer. We know what you're thinking: if it works so well on urine on porous surfaces, why not let it soak up the urine in the litter box? Because Powder Fusion is designed to clean urine from carpets, fabrics, mattresses and other porous surfaces, not to live in your litter box. And you definitely don't want your cat associating that scent with their bathroom. Clean the bed today, and you could accidentally create the world's biggest litter box tomorrow! When used as directed, Powder Fusion is safe to use around pets and children. After applying, cover the area with a towel so your pet doesn't walk through the powder. Then vacuum thoroughly and wipe with a damp cloth to remove any remaining residue. Keep it Shady, but keep it out of the litter box!

Does it really work?

Be honest... can this stuff handle the wildest, strongest, most terrifying pet odors imaginable? (Like... coyote level?)

We don't just handle it; we humiliate it. We have literally tested our formula on actual coyote urine, which is basically the final boss of pet odors, and it completely vaporized the scent! We caught the whole experiment on camera. We even had an oblivious bystander smell the test patch right after, and they thought it smelled fantastic! If our system can look a coyote mess in the eye and destroy it, your fluffy little house cat doesn't stand a chance. Don't fake the funk. Destroy it!

Every company claims their product works, but what happens when it rains? Is that awful smell going to creep back up the next time it gets humid?

We don't fake the funk, we destroy it for good! Old smells ghost you on rainy or humid days with other products because of terrible mechanics. Scented sprays just perfume the surface, creating a horrific chemical and urine hybrid scent. Unscented oxygen sprays are just as bad: they tell you to blast the spot with 20 to 30 heavy shots and walk away. All that does is pool the liquid, pushing the biological disaster deep into your carpet backing and subfloor to lie in wait. The second humidity fills the air, those unextracted crystals wake right back up! And whatever you do, never hit it with a steam cleaner first. The heat will cook the proteins in the urine, permanently sealing the odor into your carpet fibers. Our system works backwards from the chaos. Step 1: Powder Fusion locks onto those crystals so you can vacuum them out before they settle. Step 2: Enzyme Fusion eats up the biological residue. Used exactly as directed, the mess is entirely gone, so your home stays fresh whether it's sunny or pouring rain!

Why are bio-enzyme cleaners considered the gold standard? Can't I just use vinegar or a basic oxygen spray?

Using vinegar or a standard oxygen spray on cat pee is like bringing a squirt gun to a laser fight! DIY vinegar tricks just create a sour, pickled-urine nightmare. Regular oxygen sprays only treat the surface stain color while leaving the root of the stink untouched deep down. Our bio-enzymes are an entirely different breed: microscopic clean-up crews that wake up, multiply and eat the organic proteins, pheromones and uric acid crystals until there is nothing left. No residue, no cover-ups. Oxygen is fantastic for brightening a stubborn surface shadow, but only after our bio-enzymes have removed the root of the problem first. (We have a specialized Oxy Fusion surface-brightening spray in our product pipeline for exactly that final touch-up. Stay tuned!)

Are all enzyme strains the same?

Heck no! Thinking all enzymes are equal is like saying a cloudy piece of driveway gravel is the same as a flawless, sparkling diamond. Most generic pet cleaners use cheap, lazy enzymes that get tired and quit before the job is done. At Shady Pets & Paws, we spared no expense for Shady Cat Enzyme Fusion. We sourced a top-tier bio-enzyme strain that is pure, powerful and tough as nails. While the other guys just mask the mess, our premium little beasts wake up hungry, dive deep and destroy the funk at the root. Don't fake the funk with gravel when you can have a diamond!

My cat is a repeat offender. They keep going back to the exact same spot on the rug. Will this stop them?

Cats go back to the same spot because their super-powered noses can smell microscopic pheromone markers that human noses miss. When you use our full system, our bio-enzymes don't just mask the scent; they feast on those hidden markers until they are gone. If they can't smell it, the "bathroom billboard" is officially taken down!

Cat behavior

Why on earth does my cat suddenly think my favorite rug is a better bathroom than their perfectly clean litter box?

Cats are tiny, furry drama critics, and peeing outside the box is their version of writing a scathing review. First, always rule out health issues with your vet! If they get a clean bill of health, your cat is likely staging a protest. It could be a dirty box, a new litter they despise, a stray cat wandering outside the window or just general stress. They are trying to communicate, and until you solve the mystery, our system will make sure their "protest zones" don't turn into permanent bathrooms.

Why is cat pee so incredibly strong compared to other messes?

Fun fact: your cat is basically carrying a tiny piece of the desert in its litter box! Domestic cats descended from ancestors adapted to dry environments, where conserving water was essential. That water-saving ability means cats produce concentrated urine, and concentrated urine means more odor packed into a surprisingly small amount. As it sits and dries, the urine breaks down and develops that unmistakable ammonia smell we all know as "cat pee." That tiny puddle may be small, but your cat's desert-survival skills made it mighty!

Be honest... how many litter boxes do I REALLY need? (My house is starting to look like a public restroom.)

The golden rule of feline feng shui is the N+1 rule. Wait, what does N+1 even mean? It means one box per cat, plus one extra. One cat needs two boxes. Two cats need three. Cats are notoriously picky about territory and cleanliness. Some refuse a box another cat stepped in, and others like one box for #1 and a separate box for #2. Ridiculous, but true! Give them options, or they'll start choosing your couch or carpets as their backup plan.

Be honest... how often do I need to clean the litter box?

If you want your cat to keep using it, scoop at least once a day, ideally twice! Would you want to use a public restroom that hasn't been flushed in 24 hours? Or worse, a week? Absolutely not, and your picky feline roommate feels the exact same way. On top of daily scooping, do a full empty, scrub-down and litter swap every two to four weeks, depending on your litter type. Keep up with the maintenance, or your cat will declare an emergency backup bathroom right in the middle of your living room rug!

How to use it

Directions

Pretest in a hidden spot for colorfastness. Use both steps on carpets, rugs, upholstery and mattresses. On sealed hard floors, use Enzyme Fusion alone. Never steam clean first: heat sets urine proteins into the fibers.

Ingredients

Powder Fusion: absorbent synthetic polymer, inorganic substrate, water, polymeric stain resist resin, preservatives and fragrance. Enzyme Fusion: water, proprietary surfactant blend, proprietary enzyme bacterial blend, fragrance, hydrogenated castor oil, opacifier.
